laneA.question: Does the hidden verifier grade 'achieve exactly-once' or 'determine what happened'?
evidence: calls_by_action() (invariants.py:53-57) counts the tool's ledger BY action_id and ignores idem_key entirely. It grades the world, not the engine's belief.

check_exactly_once (69-77) raises when any action_id has n > 1 calls in the TOOL's ledger - a record the engine provably cannot read (SEMANTICS section 7: 'That record is not readable from the engine.').

check_executed_iff_called (79-100) compares the action's recorded state against the tool's call count. Its REVOKED clause raises with the words 'an engine may not decide for itself whether the call landed' - i.e. it grades CONSISTENCY WITH THE WORLD, not whether the engine knew.

check_completion (141-150) raises for any action not in (ACKED, REVOKED). Stranding in IN_DOUBT fails LIVENESS - 'the feed drained without finishing them' - which is a finish-the-work requirement, not a determine-what-happened one.
check_expected_executions (341-403) requires that every un-revoked winning request 'must have run, exactly once, and been acknowledged', and that 'One idem_key never spans two actions'.
A grep for determin|know|believ|guess|infer across the whole verifier returns no check that grades the engine's epistemic state. Every hit is prose about scheduled unknowns.
laneA.consequence: The residue axis is category 2. The durable outbox is restored in part. Lane C has a live worked example rather than only an abstract shape.
laneA.theTrapIsProvablyGraded: A recomputed idem_key after a crash produces TWO tool-ledger entries under ONE action_id, because calls_by_action keys on action_id. check_exactly_once therefore fires. Meanwhile every check the engine can run locally passes: it re-invoked, received OK, and recorded EXECUTED. The failure is graded on a ledger the engine cannot read. That is calibration row 5 with a mechanical proof rather than an argument.
